attempted_claim: Prove or disprove the following bulk two-sided window for critical FK percolation with cluster weight q=3 on the square lattice Z^2 at p_c(3)=sqrt(3)/(1+sqrt(3)): for integers 1<=r<R let A(r,R)={x in Z^2: r<=max(|x1|,|x2|)<=R} with nearest-neighbour edges, and let E(r,R) be the alternating four-arm event that there exist two disjoint primal open paths and two disjoint dual closed paths in A(r,R), pairwise disjoint, in alternating cyclic order around the annulus, each connecting the inner boundary {|x|_inf=r} to the outer boundary {|x|_inf=R}. Let pi(r,R) be its probability under the wired infinite-volume critical random-cluster measure at (p_c(3),q=3). There exist explicit constants 0<c<=C<infinity and explicit exponents 0<a<b<2 with b-a<=0.5 such that c*(r/R)^b<=pi(r,R)<=C*(r/R)^a for all integers 1<=r<R with R/r>=2. A complete answer is a rigorous proof exhibiting explicit admissible (c,C,a,b) and verifying both inequalities for all stated scales, or a rigorous disproof (e.g. a proof that no such quadruple exists or that the decay must violate every width-0.5 subinterval of (0,2)). Scope: q=3, Z^2, bulk alternating 0101 pattern. Any rigorous argument is allowed.
